sentences.text: The facts leading to the filing of the present petition are that the petitioners were interested persons being owner and in possession of land bearing Khasra No.1115/991/450 admeasuring 9 biswa i.e. approximately 450 sq. yds. situated at Village Chandrawali, known as Railway Road Shahdara which was acquired vide award No.1/1999-2000.
The petitioners further contended that the land use of their property was commercial and the entire area acquired vide the above award was commercial in nature.
The petitioners further contended that their land adjoins the Main GT Road which leads from ISBT Delhi to Mohan Nagar Ghaziabad.
The petitioners further contended that the market value assessed by the LAC was very low and was not the actual market value prevailing in the area as on the date of notification U/s 4 of LA Act.

It has further been further averred by the petitioners in the reference petition that father of the petitioner no.1 to 3 and grandfather of petitioner no.4 and 5 Sh. Asa Ram Gupta was the owner of the land bearing Khasra No. 1115/991/450(1-13) situated in the revenue estate of Village Chandrawali, Delhi.
It is further stated that Sh. Asa Ram Gupta died on 12.02.1981 in Delhi leaving behind the petitioners as his legal heirs.
The land was acquired vide above said award and LAC had awarded market value of the land to the tune of Rs.2805/- per sq. yards and Rs.40,000/- being value of the structure.
It is further stated that the LAC has not assessed the market value according to its situation and potential value and has not assessed true value of the structure.
Therefore, on the abovesaid grounds, the petitioners prayed for proper determination of market value of the acquired land and structure thereof.

4 The notification dated 12.06.1997 under Section 4 of the L.A. Act, 1894 was issued by the Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter referred to as "LAC") for acquisition of the acquired property for the purpose of Mass Rapid Transport System [MRTS], Delhi at Chandrawali @ Shahdara which was followed by the Notification dated 28.07.1997 under Section 6 & 17(1) of L.A. Act, 1894.

Keeping in view the use of the land under acquisition, residential L&DO rates which were issued by the Ministry of Urban Development pertaining to different areas of Delhi w.e.f. 1.4.1996 for Zone 5 was assessed by the LAC and accordingly the LAC assessed an amount of Rs.2,805/- per sq. mtrs.

Further,
solatium at the rate of 30% of market value alongwith the additional amount @ 12% of market value w.e.f. 12.06.1997 to 20.07.1999 was allowed apart from cost of structure appended to the said land Sh. sentences.text: Thus, an Award for total amount of Rs.18,48,55,526/- was passed by the LAC.
5 Being aggrieved from the lesser rate fixed by the LAC for the acquired land, the petitioner filed a petition under Section 18 of L.A. Act, 1894 before the LAC.

The LAC sent the present reference petition to this court for adjudication and court notices were issued to the parties and thereafter, on 21.01.2008, DMRC was impleaded as necessary and proper party in this reference being the beneficiary of the acquired land.

Subsequently the present case was listed for trial and finally after adjudication of the evidence filed by all the parties, Ld. Predecessor of this court finally announced an award/ judgment dated 23.09.2016 in which he relied upon the circle rates notified under the provisions of Delhi Stamp [Prevention of Undervaluation of Instruments] Rules 2007 and enhanced the market value from Rs.2805/- to Rs.5865/- per sq. mtrs..

sentences.text:
6 Respondent no.1 i.e. Union of India had filed its written statement thereby taking preliminary objections therein that Khasra number and extent of land of the petitioners are admitted to the extent of statement under Section 19 of the LAC Act; that fair, reasonable and adequate market value is always a question of fact, depending upon the evidence and onus of claiming higher compensation is always on the claimant; that the petitioners have not brought any specific and cogent evidence on record to claim a higher compensation and as such the award passed by the LAC is reasoned one, considering the market value as on the date of notification under Section 4 of the LA Act and prayed for dismissal of the reference.
7 Respondent no.2 i.e. DMRC had failed to file its written statement despite giving sufficient opportunities, therefore, right of the respondent no.2 to file the written statement was closed vide order dated 28.07.2008.
8
The present case has been passed through two rounds of litigation.

My Ld. Predecessor had already determined/assessed the market value of the acquired property @ Rs.5865/- per sq. mtrs.
vide judgment and decree dated 23.09.2016.

The said judgment was passed on the basis of market value assessed on the basis of the judgment passed in case titled Chandra Pratap Singh Vs. UOI &
Anr. which was in respect of award No.2/07-08, Jhilmil Tahirpur Delhi wherein the date of notification was 12.04.2006.

1
What was the market value of the land in question at the time of issuance of notification under Section 4 of the LA Act?
Onus on parties.

In earlier proceedings, the petitioners examined Sh. Anand Prakash Gupta, petitioner no.2, as PW1.
12
On the other hand, ld. counsel for the Union of India/respondent no.1 tendered the copy of the award no.1/1999- 2000 pertaining to Village Chandrawali as Ex.R1 in evidence.

13 It is matter of record that during the course of the proceedings, the petitioner no.1 expired and his legal heirs were impleaded as petitioners on allowing application under Order 22 Rule 3 CPC vide order dated 31.05.2019.
Amended memo of parties was filed on behalf of petitioners which was taken on record.
14 The petitioners and respondent no.1 did not lead any additional evidence and their counsel closed petitioners' evidence on 27.09.2019.
Ld. counsel for respondent no.1 also closed evidence of respondent no.1 on 27.09.2019 itself.
Thereafter, matter was fixed for evidence of respondent no.2.
15 On 13.12.2019, Sh. Vijay Kumar, Section Officer (Legal), DMRC tendered in evidence certified copies of sale deeds which are Ex.R2W1/1 to Ex.R2W1/12.
Thereafter, the evidence of respondent no.2 was closed on 13.12.2019 and matter was fixed for final arguments.
16 After conclusion of additional evidence of both the parties matter was fixed for final arguments.
17 Ld. counsels for all the parties have filed their written arguments in support of their respective stands and they submitted that they do not want to submit anything else beyond written arguments.
18 I have perused the written arguments as filed by the parties and also perused the record.

On perusal of record, my issue-wise finding is as follows:-
19

During the course of trial, the parties have apprised this court that the market value with respect to the property acquired vide the same notification and same award has already been decided by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi vide judgment dated 07.06.2019 passed in case titled UOI Vs. M.L.
Gupta & Ors. in which the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi was pleased to fix the market value of the properties acquired vide the same notification and same award @ Rs.4692/- per sq. mtr. along with statutory benefits.

The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi was pleased to assess the said market value after allowing a reduction of 20% on the rate of Rs.5865/- per sq. mtrs. which was previously determined by my Ld. Predecessor.

20 The petitioners have contended in his written arguments that the rate of Rs.5865/- per sq. mtrs.
was assessed by my ld. Predecessor on the basis of judgment passed in case titled Chandra Pratap Singh Vs. UOI in which the market value was assessed as Rs.21,920/- per sq. mtrs.

however the said market value has now been enhanced to Rs.48,000/- per sq. mtrs. and based on the said analogy,
the market value of the petitioner ought not to be less than Rs.25,000/- per sq. mtrs.

sentences.text:
Be that as it may, this court is not inclined to go into any evidence or judgment subsequent to the passing of the judgment by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case titled UOI Vs. M.L. Gupta (Supra) wherein the market value for the properties acquired vide the same notification and same award have already been assessed @ Rs.4692/- per sq. mtrs. as on the date of notification i.e.
12.06.1997.
22

The respondent no.2 has further argued that an SLP is still pending before the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India with respect to the determination of market value, however from the perusal of the record, it is apparent that the SLP filed by the respondents has been dismissed however the SLP filed by the petitioner therein namely Sh. M.L. Gupta is still pending adjudication.
Thus the market value assessed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has reached finality qua the respondents.
RELIEF 23

In view of the above noted findings, LRs of petitioner no.1 and petitioners no.2 to 5 are entitled to the market value @ Rs.4,692/- per sq. mtrs. as on 12.06.1997 with respect to their land acquired as per the statement U/s 19 of the LA Act.

In addition, LRs of petitioner no.1 and petitioners no.2 to 5 would also be entitled to all statutory benefits i.e. 30% solatium on the market value in view of the compulsory nature of acquisition U/s 23 (2) of the LA Act.

LRs of petitioner no.1 and petitioners no.2 to 5 would be entitled to additional amount @ 12% per annum U/s 23 (1A) of the LA Act from the date of notification U/s 4 of the LA Act i.e. 12.06.1997 till the date of dispossession i.e. 20.07.1999.

Besides this, LRs of petitioner no.1 and petitioners no.2 to 5 would also be entitled to interest on the enhanced amount of compensation @ 9% per annum on excess amount awarded by the court for one year from the date of notification and thereafter @ 15% per annum till the date of payment of the balance amount.

The respondents no.1 & 2 shall be jointly and severally liable to make the payment of the enhanced amount of compensation as determined herein-above to the LRs of petitioner no.1 and petitioners no.2 to 5 24

The perusal of the record shows that the respondent no.2 has already deposited the enhanced amount of compensation @
Rs.5865/- per sq. mtrs.
and therefore I hereby direct that any balance amount, after payable of the decreetal amount to the petitioners, be sent back to the respondent no.2.
If however, additional amount requires to be deposited by the respondent no.2 in terms of the present judgment, the same be remitted by the respondent no.2 with immediate effect.
25 The reference petition stands answered accordingly.
Both the sides will bear their own costs.
Decree sheet be prepared accordingly.
26 A copy of this judgement be sent to the concerned LAC for information and necessary compliance within three months of its receipt.
File be consigned to Record Room as per rules.
